newsitem.title: USA: Rain slows Nebraska corn seedings, 30 pct planted.
newsitem.headline: Rain slows Nebraska corn seedings, 30 pct planted.

text.p: Nebraska corn plantings were 30 percent complete as of Sunday, trailing last year's 55 percent as rains slowed progress in the last part of the week, according to the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service.

"Planting activities were in full swing in the first part of the week until rains limited fieldwork," the report said. "Planting activities continued to be most advanced in the south-central with 61 percent of the crop in the ground."
Oats were 87 percent planted, down from 99 percent last year and 89 percent for the five-year average. The crop was 43 percent emerged compared to 73 percent last year.
Winter wheat conditions declined from the previous week with two percent rated very poor, nine percent poor, 33 percent fair, 50 percent good and six percent excellent.
Pasture and range conditions also dropped slightly from the previous week with six percent rated very poor, 26 percent fair, 64 percent good and four percent excellent.
"Pasture growth was limited," the report said. "Warmer temperatures were needed to promote growth. "
Topsoil moisture ws rated nil very short, eight percent short, 72 percent adequate and 20 percent surplus.
